column1: # Single GEMM / convolution, strict f32, batch 1. One process per measurement; one timing protocol on all three GPUs.
# RX 7900 XT (gfx1100, RADV Mesa 26.0.8, PyTorch 2.13.0+rocm7.2, Ryzen 5 9600X), October 31, 2026; Meganeura outputs sample-checked against CPU f64.
# RTX 5070 (driver 595, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130) and Arc B570 (Mesa ANV, PyTorch 2.13.0+xpu), i5-12400F, October 31, 2026.
# Meganeura with examples/op_bench.rs; MEGANEURA_TUNE=1 (2 s kernel tuner, 64 MiB scratch; the 4096 GEMM exceeds it) MEGANEURA_DISABLE_COOP=1.
#   e40648f (5b232bd plus the tuner scratch fix, which makes the 2048 GEMM fit) on all three GPUs; each row has the median gpu_ms of 3 processes
#   (the tuner can pick different tiles per process; small B570 ops vary by up to 45%). RX 7900 XT run from branch e2f58e4, same runtime code.
#   gpu_ms = median over 30 profiled steps of summed Vulkan pass timestamps (excludes gaps between passes).
# PyTorch: TF32 off, cudnn.benchmark on, profiler off during timing (profiling perturbs ROCm execution).
#   gpu_ms = device events around one replay of a graph of 30 serial ops / 30, median of 30 replays (includes device dispatch gaps,
#   excludes host enqueue gaps). Graph outputs match eager within 1e-6 relative (bitwise except last-bit XPU differences).
# wall_ms is not comparable across engines: Meganeura's wall loop runs with MEGANEURA_GPU_TIMING=1; PyTorch's is ordinary eager calls.
# tflops = GEMM or direct-convolution FLOPs / gpu_ms (effective for Winograd). Pass labels: MatMul[MxNxK]. Inputs differ between engines.
# gemm dims: M K N; conv dims: Cin H W Cout k stride pad (data/op-bench/shapes.txt).
